sanskrit: evaṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānām āśramāṇāṃ pravṛttiṣu ekam ālambamānānāṃ nirṇaye kiṃ nirāmayam
english: Among the prescribed observances of the four orders and the four stages of life, when men hold fast to a single one of them, what in the final determination is flawless and free of ill?

sanskrit: kapila uvāca yad yad ācarate śāstram atha sarvapravṛttiṣu yasya yatra hy anuṣṭhānaṃ tatra tatra nirāmayam
english: Kapila said: Whatever course the scripture enjoins amid all undertakings—wherever a man's practice falls, there and there alone lies that which is flawless and free of ill.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ pāvayate jñānaṃ yo jñānaṃ hy anuvartate jñānād apetya yā vṛttiḥ sā vināśayati prajāḥ
english: Knowledge purifies all things for one who follows after knowledge; but the way of life that departs from knowledge destroys its creatures.

sanskrit: bhavanto jñānino nityaṃ sarvataś ca nirāgamāḥ aikātmyaṃ nāma kaś cid dhi kadā cid abhipadyate
english: You who are ever possessed of knowledge are, in every respect, beyond the bounds of scripture; yet only some rare man, only at some rare moment, attains that oneness of the self.

sanskrit: śāstraṃ hy abuddhvā tattvena ke cid vādabalā janāḥ kāmadveṣābhibhūtatvād ahaṃkāravaśaṃ gatāḥ
english: For some men, who have not grasped the scripture in its truth and rely only on the force of argument, fall under the sway of egoism, overpowered as they are by desire and hatred.

sanskrit: yāthātathyam avijñāya śāstrāṇāṃ śāstradasyavaḥ brahmastenā nirārambhā apakvamatayo 'śivāḥ
english: Not having understood the scriptures as they truly are, they become robbers of scripture, thieves of the sacred word—men who undertake nothing, whose minds are unripe and whose ways are inauspicious.

sanskrit: vaiguṇyam eva paśyanti na guṇān anuyuñjate teṣāṃ tamaḥśarīrāṇāṃ tama eva parāyaṇam
english: They see only fault and do not seek out the virtues; for such men, whose very bodies are made of darkness, darkness alone is their final refuge.

sanskrit: yo yathāprakṛtir jantuḥ prakṛteḥ syād vaśānugaḥ tasya dveṣaś ca kāmaś ca krodho dambho 'nṛtaṃ madaḥ nityam evābhivartante guṇāḥ prakṛtisaṃbhavāḥ
english: Whatever a creature's inborn nature, if he remains subject to that nature's sway, then hatred and desire, anger, deceit, falsehood, and pride—the strands of being born of his nature—ever rise up and overwhelm him.

sanskrit: etad buddhyānupaśyantaḥ saṃtyajeyuḥ śubhāśubham parāṃ gatim abhīpsanto yatayaḥ saṃyame ratāḥ
english: Perceiving this with the understanding, the ascetics who delight in self-restraint and long for the supreme goal should renounce alike the auspicious and the inauspicious.

sanskrit: syūmaraśmir uvāca sarvam etan mayā brahmañ śāstrataḥ parikīrtitam na hy avijñāya śātrārthaṃ pravartante pravṛttayaḥ
english: Syūmaraśmi said: All this, O brahman, has been proclaimed by me on the authority of scripture; for no undertakings are set in motion without one's having understood the purport of scripture.

sanskrit: yaḥ kaś cin nyāyya ācāraḥ sarvaṃ śāstram iti śrutiḥ yad anyāyyam aśāstraṃ tad ity eṣā śrūyate śrutiḥ
english: Whatever conduct is righteous is in its entirety scripture—so declares the sacred tradition; and whatever is unrighteous is contrary to scripture—this too is the tradition that is heard.

sanskrit: na pravṛttir ṛte śāstrāt kā cid astīti niścayaḥ yad anyad vedavādebhyas tad aśāstram iti śrutiḥ
english: It is settled that no activity whatsoever exists apart from scripture; and whatever is other than the teachings of the Veda is contrary to scripture—so runs the tradition.

sanskrit: śāstrād apetaṃ paśyanti bahavo vyaktamāninaḥ śāstradoṣān na paśyanti iha cāmutra cāpare avijñānahataprajñā hīnaprajñās tamovṛtāḥ
english: Many who fancy themselves clear-sighted look upon things as set apart from scripture; while others, here and in the world beyond, fail to see the faults that come of forsaking it—men whose discernment is slain by ignorance, of meager wit and shrouded in darkness.

sanskrit: śakyaṃ tv ekena muktena kṛtakṛtyena sarvaśaḥ piṇḍamātraṃ vyapāśritya carituṃ sarvatodiśam vedavādaṃ vyapāśritya mokṣo 'stīti prabhāṣitum
english: It is indeed possible for one man, set free, who has wholly accomplished his task, to wander in every direction relying on no more than a morsel of food; and leaning upon the teaching of the Veda, to declare that liberation exists.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu duṣkaraṃ karma kuṭumbam abhisaṃśritam dānam adhyayanaṃ yajñaḥ prajāsaṃtānam ārjavam
english: But this is hard work that the householder takes upon himself, bound to family and home: gift-giving, the study of the sacred texts, sacrifice, the continuance of offspring, and uprightness.

sanskrit: yady etad evaṃ kṛtvāpi na vimokṣo 'sti kasya cit dhik kartāraṃ ca kāryaṃ ca śramaś cāyaṃ nirarthakaḥ
english: If, even after a man has done all this, there is no liberation for anyone, then fie upon the doer and the deed alike, and all this toil is to no purpose.

sanskrit: nāstikyam anyathā ca syād vedānāṃ pṛṣṭhataḥkriyā etasyānantyam icchāmi bhagavañ śrotum añjasā
english: Otherwise there would be denial of the divine and a casting of the Vedas behind one's back. Of this, O blessed one, I wish to hear the unending truth, plainly and at once.

sanskrit: tathyaṃ vadasva me brahmann upasanno 'smy adhīhi bhoḥ yathā te vidito mokṣas tathecchāmy upaśikṣitum
english: Tell me the truth, O brahman; I have come to you as a suppliant—teach me, sir. As liberation is known to you, even so I wish to be instructed in it.

sanskrit: kapila uvāca vedāḥ pramāṇaṃ lokānāṃ na vedāḥ pṛṣṭhataḥkṛtāḥ dve brahmaṇī veditavye śabdabrahma paraṃ ca yat śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati
english: Kapila said: The Vedas are the measure of all the worlds, and the Vedas are not cast behind one's back. Two Absolutes are to be known: the Absolute that is sound, and that which is supreme; and one who is well-versed in the Absolute that is sound attains the supreme Absolute.

sanskrit: śarīram etat kurute yad vede kurute tanum kṛtaśuddhaśarīro hi pātraṃ bhavati brāhmaṇaḥ
english: That which a man fashions in accordance with the Veda fashions his body and gives it form; for only when his body has been made pure does the brahman become a fit vessel.

sanskrit: ānantyam anuyuṅkte yaḥ karmaṇā tad bravīmi te nirāgamam anaitihyaṃ pratyakṣaṃ lokasākṣikam
english: Of him who, through his action, pursues the infinite, I now speak to you—a truth needing no scriptural support, no hearsay, but plain to perception and witnessed by all the world.

sanskrit: dharma ity eva ye yajñān vitanvanti nirāśiṣaḥ utpannatyāgino 'lubdhāḥ kṛpāsūyāvivarjitāḥ dhanānām eṣa vai panthās tīrtheṣu pratipādanam
english: Those who spread out their sacrifices solely for the sake of righteousness, free of craving for reward, given to renunciation as it arises, untouched by greed, and devoid of pity-seeking and spite—for them this is the true path of wealth: its bestowal upon worthy recipients at the holy fords.

sanskrit: anāśritāḥ pāpakṛtyāḥ kadā cit karmayonitaḥ manaḥsaṃkalpasaṃsiddhā viśuddhajñānaniścayāḥ
english: Resting on nothing, they are never given to evil deeds, even from the source whence action springs; they are perfected by the resolve of their own minds, settled in the certitude of utterly pure knowledge.

sanskrit: akrudhyanto 'nasūyanto nirahaṃkāramatsarāḥ jñānaniṣṭhās triśuklāś ca sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ
english: Free of anger, free of malice, without egoism or envy, fixed in knowledge, threefold pure, they delight in the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: āsan gṛhasthā bhūyiṣṭham avyutkrāntāḥ svakarmasu rājānaś ca tathā yuktā brāhmaṇāś ca yathāvidhi
english: For the most part they were householders, never swerving from their own duties; and likewise the kings were yoked to their tasks, and the brahmans too, each according to rule.

sanskrit: samā hy ārjavasaṃpannāḥ saṃtuṣṭā jñānaniścayāḥ pratyakṣadharmāḥ śucayaḥ śraddadhānāḥ parāvare
english: Even-minded, endowed with uprightness, content, settled in knowledge, with righteousness made manifest before them, pure and full of faith in the higher and the lower alike.

sanskrit: purastād bhāvitātmāno yathāvac caritavratāḥ caranti dharmaṃ kṛcchre 'pi durge caivādhisaṃhatāḥ
english: From the first their souls were refined, their vows duly fulfilled; and even in hardship and dire straits, banded firmly together, they walk in the way of righteousness.

sanskrit: saṃhatya dharmaṃ caratāṃ purāsīt sukham eva tat teṣāṃ nāsīd vidhātavyaṃ prāyaścittaṃ kadā cana
english: For those who in former times walked together in righteousness, that itself was happiness; for them there was never any penance that needed to be ordained.

sanskrit: satyaṃ hi dharmam āsthāya durādharṣatamā matāḥ na mātrām anurudhyante na dharmacchalam antataḥ
english: For, taking their stand upon truth and righteousness, they were held to be most unassailable; they yielded not even to a hair's breadth of compromise, nor in the end to any sham of righteousness.

sanskrit: ya eva prathamaḥ kalpas tam evābhyācaran saha asyāṃ sthitau sthitānāṃ hi prāyaścittaṃ na vidyate durbalātmana utpannaṃ prāyaścittam iti śrutiḥ
english: Whatever was the foremost rule, that very rule they all practiced together; for those who stand firm in this state, no penance is to be found. Penance arose for the weak of soul—so runs the tradition.

sanskrit: yata evaṃvidhā viprāḥ purāṇā yajñavāhanāḥ traividyavṛddhāḥ śucayo vṛttavanto yaśasvinaḥ yajanto 'har ahar yajñair nirāśīrbandhanā budhāḥ
english: For brahmans of this kind in olden days were the bearers of sacrifice, grown old in the threefold lore, pure, of good conduct and great renown, offering sacrifices day after day—wise men freed from the bonds of craving.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ yajñāś ca vedāś ca karmāṇi ca yathāgamam āgamāś ca yathākālaṃ saṃkalpāś ca yathāvratam
english: Their sacrifices, their Vedas, and their rites were all according to scripture; their sacred recitations were according to the appointed seasons, and their resolves according to their vows.

sanskrit: apetakāmakrodhānāṃ prakṛtyā saṃśitātmanām ṛjūnāṃ śamanityānāṃ sthitānāṃ sveṣu karmasu sarvam ānantyam evāsīd iti naḥ śāśvatī śrutiḥ
english: For men who had cast off desire and anger, whose selves were by nature keen and disciplined, upright, ever tranquil, steadfast in their own duties—all was the infinite itself: so runs the eternal tradition handed down to us.

sanskrit: teṣām adīnasattvānāṃ duścarācārakarmaṇām svakarmabhiḥ saṃvṛtānāṃ tapo ghoratvam āgatam
english: For those of undaunted spirit, whose conduct and works were hard to pursue, who were wholly compassed by their own duties, their austerity attained a fearsome intensity.

sanskrit: taṃ sadācāram āścaryaṃ purāṇaṃ śāśvataṃ dhruvam aśaknuvadbhiś carituṃ kiṃ cid dharmeṣu sūcitam
english: That conduct of the virtuous—wondrous, ancient, everlasting, and fixed—has been but faintly indicated among the duties, for those who cannot practice it in full.

sanskrit: nirāpaddharma ācāras tv apramādo 'parābhavaḥ sarvavarṇeṣu yat teṣu nāsīt kaś cid vyatikramaḥ
english: Their conduct was a righteousness free of calamity, free of negligence, free of defeat; and among them, in all the orders, there was never any transgression.

sanskrit: dharmam ekaṃ catuṣpādam āśritās te nararṣabhāḥ taṃ santo vidhivat prāpya gacchanti paramāṃ gatim
english: Those bulls among men held fast to the one righteousness of four feet; and the good, attaining it duly, go to the supreme goal.

sanskrit: gṛhebhya eva niṣkramya vanam anye samāśritāḥ gṛham evābhisaṃśritya tato 'nye brahmacāriṇaḥ
english: Some, going forth from their homes, betook themselves to the forest; others, abiding in the household itself, were thereafter chaste students of the sacred lore.

sanskrit: dharmam etaṃ catuṣpādam āśramaṃ brāhmaṇā viduḥ ānantyaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ brāhmaṇā nāma niścayaḥ
english: This righteousness of four feet the brahmans know as the system of life-stages; the infinite is the abode of the Absolute—the brahmans, in truth, are its certitude.

sanskrit: ata evaṃvidhā viprāḥ purāṇā dharmacāriṇaḥ ta ete divi dṛśyante jyotirbhūtā dvijātayaḥ
english: And so those brahmans of olden days, of this kind, walkers in the way of righteousness—these very twice-born ones are seen in heaven, become lights in the sky.

sanskrit: nakṣatrāṇīva dhiṣṇyeṣu bahavas tārakāgaṇāḥ ānantyam upasaṃprāptāḥ saṃtoṣād iti vaidikam
english: Like the constellations in their stations, like the manifold hosts of stars, they have attained the infinite through contentment—so the Vedic teaching declares.

sanskrit: yady āgacchanti saṃsāraṃ punar yoniṣu tādṛśāḥ na lipyante pāpakṛtyaiḥ kadā cit karmayonitaḥ
english: And if such men come again into the round of rebirths, into the wombs once more, they are never stained by evil deeds, even from the source whence action springs.

sanskrit: evaṃ yukto brāhmaṇaḥ syād anyo brāhmaṇako bhavet karmaiva puruṣasyāha śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham
english: A brahman thus disciplined is a brahman indeed; another is but a brahman in name only. It is a man's action alone that proclaims him, whether for good or for ill.

sanskrit: evaṃ pakvakaṣāyāṇām ānantyena śrutena ca sarvam ānantyam evāsīd evaṃ naḥ śāśvatī śrutiḥ
english: Thus for those whose impurities have been ripened away, through the infinite and through sacred learning, all was the infinite itself: such is the eternal tradition handed down to us.

sanskrit: teṣām apetatṛṣṇānāṃ nirṇiktānāṃ śubhātmanām caturtha aupaniṣado dharmaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: For those who have put away thirst, who are washed clean, of auspicious soul, the fourth duty—that of the Upaniṣads—is remembered as common to all.

sanskrit: sa siddhaiḥ sādhyate nityaṃ brāhmaṇair niyatātmabhiḥ saṃtoṣamūlas tyāgātmā jñānādhiṣṭhānam ucyate
english: It is ever brought to perfection by the perfected, by brahmans of disciplined self; rooted in contentment, its essence renunciation, it is called the very seat of knowledge.

sanskrit: apavargagatir nityo yatidharmaḥ sanātanaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ kevalo vā yathābalam upāsyate
english: The way of final release, eternal, is the everlasting duty of the ascetic; whether held in common or kept alone, it is practiced according to one's strength.

sanskrit: gacchato gacchataḥ kṣemaṃ durbalo 'trāvasīdati brahmaṇaḥ padam anvicchan saṃsārān mucyate śuciḥ
english: As one goes ever onward toward security, the weak man here sinks down by the way; but he who, seeking the station of the Absolute and remaining pure, is freed from the round of rebirths.

sanskrit: syūmaraśmir uvāca ye bhuñjate ye dadate yajante 'dhīyate ca ye mātrābhir dharmalabdhābhir ye vā tyāgaṃ samāśritāḥ
english: Syūmaraśmi said: Those who enjoy, those who give, those who sacrifice and who study, who do so with the means righteously obtained, or those who have taken to renunciation—

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ pretyabhāve tu katamaḥ svargajittamaḥ etad ācakṣva me brahman yathātathyena pṛcchataḥ
english: of these, in the life after death, which is the most victorious in winning heaven? Tell me this, O brahman, in its very truth, for I ask it.

sanskrit: kapila uvāca parigrahāḥ śubhāḥ sarve guṇato 'bhyudayāś ca ye na tu tyāgasukhaṃ prāptā etat tvam api paśyasi
english: Kapila said: All possessions are good, and so are the prosperities that come of merit; yet they do not attain the happiness of renunciation—this too you can see for yourself.

sanskrit: syūmaraśmir uvāca bhavanto jñānaniṣṭhā vai gṛhasthāḥ karmaniścayāḥ āśramāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ niṣṭhāyām aikyam ucyate
english: Syūmaraśmi said: You are firmly grounded in knowledge, while householders are settled in action; yet in their consummation a oneness is said to belong to all the life-stages.

sanskrit: ekatve ca pṛthaktve ca viśeṣo nānya ucyate tad yathāvad yathānyāyaṃ bhagavān prabravītu me
english: As to their oneness and their distinctness, no other difference is spoken of. Let the blessed one declare this to me duly and according to reason.

sanskrit: kapila uvāca śarīrapaktiḥ karmāṇi jñānaṃ tu paramā gatiḥ pakve kaṣāye vamanai rasajñāne na tiṣṭhati
english: Kapila said: Rites are the ripening of the body, but knowledge is the supreme goal. When the impurity has been ripened away through the purgings, one no longer abides in the mere savoring of relish.

sanskrit: ānṛśaṃsyaṃ kṣamā śāntir ahiṃsā satyam ārjavam adroho nābhimānaś ca hrīs titikṣā śamas tathā
english: Freedom from cruelty, forbearance, peace, non-injury, truth, uprightness, freedom from malice and from arrogance, modesty, endurance, and tranquility—

sanskrit: panthāno brahmaṇas tv ete etaiḥ prāpnoti yat param tad vidvān anubudhyeta manasā karmaniścayam
english: these are the paths to the Absolute; by these a man attains what is supreme. Knowing this, let the wise man comprehend in his mind the true ground of action.

sanskrit: yāṃ viprāḥ sarvataḥ śāntā viśuddhā jñānaniścayāḥ gatiṃ gacchanti saṃtuṣṭās tām āhuḥ paramāṃ gatim
english: That goal to which the brahmans, tranquil in every way, utterly pure, settled in knowledge and content, attain—that they call the supreme goal.

sanskrit: vedāṃś ca veditavyaṃ ca viditvā ca yathāsthiti evaṃ vedavid ity āhur ato 'nyo vātareṭakaḥ
english: Having known the Vedas and that which is to be known, each in its proper standing—such a man they call a knower of the Veda; one other than this is but a windbag.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ vidur vedavido vede sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam vede hi niṣṭhā sarvasya yad yad asti ca nāsti ca
english: The knowers of the Veda know all; in the Veda all is established. For in the Veda is the ground of everything, whatever exists and whatever does not.

sanskrit: eṣaiva niṣṭhā sarvasya yad yad asti ca nāsti ca etad antaṃ ca madhyaṃ ca sac cāsac ca vijānataḥ
english: This is the very ground of everything, whatever exists and whatever does not; this is the end and the middle, the real and the unreal, for one who truly discerns.

sanskrit: samastatyāga ity eva śama ity eva niṣṭhitaḥ saṃtoṣa ity atra śubham apavarge pratiṣṭhitam
english: It rests in total renunciation, and in tranquility; here the good lies in contentment, and it is established in final release.

sanskrit: ṛtaṃ satyaṃ viditaṃ veditavyaṃ; sarvasyātmā jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ ca sarvaṃ sukhaṃ yac chivam uttamaṃ ca; brahmāvyaktaṃ prabhavaś cāvyayaś ca
english: It is the cosmic order, the truth, the known and the yet-to-be-known; the Self of all, both the moving and the unmoving; it is all happiness, and that which is auspicious and supreme—the Absolute, the unmanifest, the source and the imperishable.

sanskrit: tejaḥ kṣamā śāntir anāmayaṃ śubhaṃ; tathāvidhaṃ vyoma sanātanaṃ dhruvam etaiḥ śabdair gamyate buddhinetrais; tasmai namo brahmaṇe brāhmaṇāya
english: It is splendor, forbearance, peace, the flawless, the auspicious; even such is that eternal, fixed expanse. By these words, with the understanding for one's eye, It is approached: to that Absolute, to that holy Power, be homage.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca vedāḥ śaṃsanti bhārata kasya lābho viśiṣṭo 'tra tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Righteousness, wealth, and pleasure—these the Vedas commend, O Bhārata. Of which is the gaining most excellent? Tell me that, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣyāmi itihāsaṃ purātanam kuṇḍadhāreṇa yat prītyā bhaktāyopakṛtaṃ purā
english: Bhīṣma said: On this I shall relate to you an ancient tale, of the kindness that Kuṇḍadhāra long ago, out of affection, did for his devotee.

sanskrit: adhano brāhmaṇaḥ kaś cit kāmād dharmam avaikṣata yajñārthaṃ sa tato 'rthārthī tapo 'tapyata dāruṇam
english: A certain penniless brahman, out of desire, looked toward righteousness; and then, longing for the means to sacrifice, he performed a terrible austerity in his craving for wealth.

sanskrit: sa niścayam atho kṛtvā pūjayām āsa devatāḥ bhaktyā na caivādhyagacchad dhanaṃ saṃpūjya devatāḥ
english: Then, having made his resolve, he worshiped the gods with devotion; yet even after worshiping the gods, he did not come upon any wealth.

sanskrit: tataś cintāṃ punaḥ prāptaḥ katamad daivataṃ nu tat yan me drutaṃ prasīdeta mānuṣair ajaḍīkṛtam
english: Then he fell again to brooding: 'Which deity might that be, who would be swiftly gracious to me—one not made dull by the worship of men?'

sanskrit: atha saumyena vapuṣā devānucaram antike pratyapaśyaj jaladharaṃ kuṇḍadhāram avasthitam
english: Then, in gentle form, he beheld close at hand an attendant of the gods, the cloud-spirit Kuṇḍadhāra, standing near.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva taṃ mahātmānaṃ tasya bhaktir ajāyata ayaṃ me dhāsyati śreyo vapur etad dhi tādṛśam
english: The moment he saw that great being, devotion was born in him: 'This one will grant me good fortune, for such indeed is his form.'

sanskrit: saṃnikṛṣṭaś ca devasya na cānyair mānuṣair vṛtaḥ eṣa me dāsyati dhanaṃ prabhūtaṃ śīghram eva ca
english: 'And he is close to the god, and not beset by other men's worship; this one will give me wealth in abundance, and that swiftly too.'

sanskrit: tato dhūpaiś ca gandhaiś ca mālyair uccāvacair api balibhir vividhaiś cāpi pūjayām āsa taṃ dvijaḥ
english: Then with incense and perfumes and garlands of every sort, and with manifold offerings, the twice-born one worshiped him.

sanskrit: tataḥ svalpena kālena tuṣṭo jaladharas tadā tasyopakāre niyatām imāṃ vācam uvāca ha
english: Then in a little while the cloud-spirit was pleased, and intent on doing him a kindness, he spoke this measured word.

sanskrit: brahmaghne ca surāpe ca core bhagnavrate tathā niṣkṛtir vihitā sadbhiḥ kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ
english: 'For the slayer of a brahman, for the drinker of liquor, for the thief, and for the breaker of vows, an expiation has been ordained by the good; but for the ingrate there is no expiation.'

sanskrit: āśāyās tanayo 'dharmaḥ krodho 'sūyāsutaḥ smṛtaḥ putro lobho nikṛtyās tu kṛtaghno nārhati prajām
english: 'Unrighteousness is the son of hope; anger is remembered as the son of envy; greed is the son of deceit—but the ingrate deserves no offspring at all.'

sanskrit: tataḥ sa brāhmaṇaḥ svapne kuṇḍadhārasya tejasā apaśyat sarvabhūtāni kuśeṣu śayitas tadā
english: Then that brahman, lying upon the kuśa grass, beheld in a dream, through Kuṇḍadhāra's power, all created beings.

sanskrit: śamena tapasā caiva bhaktyā ca nirupaskṛtaḥ śuddhātmā brāhmaṇo rātrau nidarśanam apaśyata
english: By tranquility, by austerity, and by devotion made unadorned and undefiled, the pure-souled brahman beheld in the night a revelation.

sanskrit: maṇibhadraṃ sa tatrasthaṃ devatānāṃ mahādyutim apaśyata mahātmānaṃ vyādiśantaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: He beheld there, O Yudhiṣṭhira, Maṇibhadra, of great splendor among the gods, that great-souled one, issuing his commands.

sanskrit: tatra devāḥ prayacchanti rājyāni ca dhanāni ca śubhaiḥ karmabhir ārabdhāḥ pracchidanty aśubheṣu ca
english: There the gods bestow kingdoms and wealth; moved by auspicious deeds they grant, and in the case of inauspicious ones they cut these off.

sanskrit: paśyatām atha yakṣāṇāṃ kuṇḍadhāro mahādyutiḥ niṣpatya patito bhūmau devānāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Then, while the yakṣas looked on, Kuṇḍadhāra of great splendor flung himself down and fell to the ground before the gods, O bull of the Bhāratas.
